findings.title: Upload page scrolls sideways on phone widths (fails the 'usable at 375 px' checklist item; contradicts step 8's note)
findings.repro: 1) python3 .../scratchpad/docgen/build_stage.py AHM-02 <new dir> (AHM-03 is the same). 2) cd <dir>; MAXGUARD_DATA_DIR=<dir>/data uvicorn maxguard.api.app:create_app --factory --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18702. 3) Playwright Chromium: browser.newContext({viewport:{width:375,height:812}}), goto http://127.0.0.1:18702/upload. 4) evaluate document.documentElement.scrollWidth: 398 (clientWidth 375). window.scrollTo(500,0) then window.scrollX: 23. The file input and the Analyze button run past the card's right edge and off-screen (screenshot upload-375-ahm02.png).
findings.evidence: pages_ahm02.json / pages_ahm03.json: '375 window analyst /upload http=200 scrollWidth=398 clientWidth=375 FAIL wide=['label right=398', 'input#file right=398', 'button right=398']' (phone emulation 399). upload_overflow_ahm02.json: gridColumns '365px' while the card is 343 px wide (309 px content box) at 375 px; 'scrollXAfterScrollTo500': 23. Why: Chromium 141.0.7390.37 sizes an empty file input from 34 '0' characters; with the default font here (fc-match system-ui = DejaVu Sans, '0' = 10.18 px), 34 x 10.18 = 346.1 px plus padding and border = 365 px. The grid's only column is auto-sized and grid items have min-width:auto, so the column cannot shrink below that, and max-width:100% on the input does not help. It depends on the font (upload_overflow_matrix.txt). DejaVu Sans scrolls sideways at 320/360/375/390 px. With Arial-metric Liberation Sans it scrolls at 320 px (scrollWidth 354, the WCAG 1.4.10 reflow width), and at 360/375 px the input sticks 12 px out of the card's content box. app.css is byte-identical in the AHM-04 and ALL builds.
findings.fix: In maxguard/web/static/app.css line 96 (docs/roadmap/ahmad.md line 882) change the rule to '.status-form, #upload-form { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 8px; max-width: 420px; }'. Verified in Chromium by injecting the rule on /upload: scrollWidth 375 at 375 px and 320 at 320 px, with both fonts. The input becomes 309 px and fits the card (upload-375-ahm02-candidate-fix.png). It also applies to .status-form, which I did not re-check in a browser with the fix (it already fits without it). With all my fixes applied in a private copy, test_web.py still gives 39 passed and ruff 'All checks passed!'. Also correct the sentence at ahmad.md:1227 ('Chromium at 375 px showed no sideways scrolling').

findings.title: Every queue refresh (the 30 s poll or alerts-changed) throws keyboard focus off the alert list
findings.repro: Build AHM-02 or AHM-03, start the server, upload tests/fixtures/zeek/telnet as a .zip. In Chromium open http://127.0.0.1:<port>/, press Tab until 'Telnet session in cleartext' (the alert link) has focus. (a) From another client change the alert, e.g. curl -X PATCH -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"actor":"x","assignee":"Another Analyst"}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/alerts/c6823b232c932762, or (b) change nothing and just wait up to 30 s. Then read document.activeElement and press Tab.
findings.evidence: focus_refresh_ahm02.json and focus_refresh_ahm03.json. before 'a[href=/alerts/c6823b232c932762] "Telnet session in cleartext"'; sseRefresh {msToRefresh 775 (AHM-02) / 765 (AHM-03), focusAfter 'BODY', nextTab 'a[href=#main] "Skip to content"'}; pollRefresh {secondsUntilPoll '28.8', focusAfter 'BODY'}. Cause: queue.html line 33 (hx-trigger="refresh, every 30s", hx-swap="outerHTML") replaces #alerts even when nothing changed. The links have no id (AHM-02 queue.html:52, AHM-03 queue.html:53; ahmad.md:736 and 1716). The vendored htmx 2.0.11 restores focus only by id: 'if(t.elt&&!ie(t.elt)&&Q(t.elt,"id")){const f=document.getElementById(Q(t.elt,"id"));...f.focus(h)}'. So a keyboard user moving through the queue is sent back to the top of the page at least every 30 s.
findings.fix: Give each alert link a stable id: '<a id="alert-{{ alert.finding_id }}" href="/alerts/{{ alert.finding_id }}">'. Verified in a private copy (focus_refresh_fixcopy.json): focusAfter 'a#alert-c6823b232c932762[...]' after both the change-driven refresh (776 ms) and the 28.8 s poll; test_web.py 39 passed. Optional: skip the swap when the table did not change.

findings.title: With 6 queue tabs open, the whole dashboard stops answering in that browser
findings.repro: Build AHM-02 or AHM-03 and start the server. In one Chromium profile open http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ in 6 tabs (wait for each tab's /api/stream to connect). Open a 7th tab at /upload, or change a filter in one of the 6 queue tabs.
findings.evidence: sse_limit.js: 5 tabs, the extra tab loaded in 35 ms (AHM-02) / 30 ms (AHM-03). 6 tabs: 'page.goto: Timeout 10000ms exceeded.' on both copies; closing one queue tab let it load in 151 / 146 ms. sse_limit_filter.js (AHM-03): filter change in tab 3 of 6, 'NO ANSWER after 8002 ms'. Cause: app.js:9-10 opens one EventSource('/api/stream') per queue tab and keeps it open forever. uvicorn serves HTTP/1.1, and Chromium allows 6 connections per host, so 6 streams leave none for page loads or htmx requests.
findings.fix: Not verified (suggestions): close the EventSource when the tab is hidden (visibilitychange) and reopen it with one refresh when visible, or share one stream across tabs (BroadcastChannel/SharedWorker), or rely on polling. At least document the limit.

result.notes:
Most things work as the guides say. Headers (step 7) match exactly. The Telnet alert appears in an open queue tab within 0.1 to 0.5 s with no reload, and the 30 s fallback works (29.6 s). Every control can be reached and used with the keyboard and the focus outline is always visible. Only 127.0.0.1 is contacted. AI citations work, and a sentence citing any ID outside the finding (even a real record from the same upload) is dropped. AI text is escaped. rows.threat: A malicious archive fills the disk (zip bomb) or writes outside its folder
rows.defense: maxguard/adapters/zeeklogs.py: _check_size() sums each member's DECLARED uncompressed size and raises ArchiveTooLarge before extracting if the sum exceeds MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES (4 GiB). _extract() then unpacks zip via zipfile.extractall (stdlib strips absolute paths and '..' parts) and tar via tarfile.extractall(filter='data') (the data filter raises for '..', symlinks, hardlinks and device/special files, and neutralizes absolute paths by stripping the leading slash so they land inside the destination). to_zeek_logs() is the single entry the pipeline and the API use for non-directory inputs. The API upload path (maxguard/api/app.py) does NOT extract itself: save_upload() writes the body under a random token_hex name with a magic-number suffix (client filename is never used as a path), and run_pipeline() delegates unpacking to the adapter via analyze(), mapping ArchiveTooLarge->413 and (zipfile.BadZipFile, tarfile.TarError, EOFError)->400. All four tar data-filter errors (OutsideDestinationError, AbsolutePathError, LinkOutsideDestinationError, SpecialFileError) subclass tarfile.TarError, so the API catches them as a clean 400 rather than a 500.
code_refs: maxguard/adapters/zeeklogs.py:96-104 (_extract: zip extractall; tar extractall filter='data')
rows.attacks: Built my own AHM-04 copy and ran, against adapters/zeeklogs.py _extract/to_zeek_logs and against the real /api/analyses endpoint (TestClient): (A) a hand-built zip whose member declares file_size=10 but whose DEFLATE stream decompresses to 20000 bytes; (B) a zip bomb member declaring 100000 bytes with MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES monkeypatched down to 10 (so no 4 GiB is ever written); (C) a zip with members named '../../<canary>/evil.log' and absolute '/etc/evil_abs.log'; (D) a tar with '../../<canary>/evil.log'; (E) a tar with absolute '/tmp/tar_evil_abs.log'; (F) a tar with a symlink -> '../../../../etc/passwd'; (G) a tar with a hard link -> '../../../../etc/passwd'; (H) a tar with a character-device TarInfo (CHRTYPE, built in Python, no root); (I) end-to-end to_zeek_logs() with '../../e2e_escape/conn.log'; and the same traversal/symlink/device archives POSTed to /api/analyses. Also tested the tar size pre-check with the limit lowered.
commands: python3 scratchpad/docgen/build_stage.py AHM-04 <repo>  # my own private copy
PYTHONPATH=repo .venv/bin/python attacks.py <scratch>   # A-I against the adapter
python - (tar oversize: MAX_EXTRACTED_BYTES=10 -> ArchiveTooLarge before extract, dest not created)
rows.observed: A: zipfile.BadZipFile 'Bad CRC-32 for file conn.log' - extractall caps output at the declared file_size then fails CRC, so a member can never write more than its declared size; the declared-size pre-check is therefore a sound upper bound. B: ArchiveTooLarge raised, destination empty (refused before any write). C: no raise, but files landed at 'ziptrav_canary/evil_rel.log' and 'etc/evil_abs.log' INSIDE dest; the outside canary dir stayed empty and /etc/evil_abs.log was not created (zipfile stripped '..' and the leading '/'). D: tarfile.OutsideDestinationError, canary empty. E: no raise; sanitized to 'tmp/tar_evil_abs.log' inside dest; /tmp/tar_evil_abs.log not created. F: tarfile.LinkOutsideDestinationError, no symlink created. G: tarfile.LinkOutsideDestinationError. H: tarfile.SpecialFileError, no device node. I: tarfile.OutsideDestinationError, e2e_escape not created outside. API /api/analyses: tar traversal/symlink/device each returned 400 ('not a valid archive: ... outside the destination' / 'is a special file'); zip traversal returned 200 with 0 findings (names neutralized, extracted inside the temp workdir, nothing escaped); the api_escape dir outside the data dir was never created; uploads were deleted. Tar oversize: ArchiveTooLarge before extract, dest not created. Python 3.11.15, so tarfile.data_filter is present and filter='data' is honored.
rows.notes: No disk-fill and no write outside the destination in any test, at both the adapter and the API layers; this is the only archive-extraction surface in the alpha (the only extractall calls are zeeklogs.py:100 and :104; no maxguard/intel/bundle.py exists in AHM-04 - the signed intel-bundle extractor is Spring 2027, a different threat row). One documentation-precision nuance, NOT a security finding: the table says the data filter 'refuses absolute paths', but on POSIX the data filter neutralizes absolute paths (strips the leading slash, extracting inside the destination) rather than raising; it raises for '..', links and device files. The zip side likewise neutralizes '..' and absolute names by stripping rather than raising. The threat the row names - writing outside the folder - is fully prevented either way.

result.extra: Row 1 (malicious archive) verified against the alpha build at scratchpad/stages/AHM-04, rebuilt into my own copy at scratchpad/agentwork/sec-archives/repo.
